answer: Make every agent key prove it trained its own model. At join, the key receives a private seed-derived dataset, fine-tunes a small LoRA adapter on it, and signs a checkpoint hash every 50 steps, a quill log kept in a public vault. Auditors replay one random 50-step segment; a mismatch voids the seat. Jurors then send secret ivory probe prompts: keys whose output distributions overlap above 0.95 merge into one seat. Each fake costs ~3 GPU-hours (~$6) per 30-day refresh, linear in N, and cloned adapters fail the probe merge.
